question: What is the main purpose of a skilled nursing facility (SNF)?

options.A: To replace standard emergency room hospital services
options.B: To act as a daycare center for healthy older adults
options.C: To offer permanent housing without medical supervision
options.D: To provide 24-hour medical care and rehabilitation

explanation: Think of a skilled nursing facility as a place for round-the-clock care and therapy when patients are recovering or need ongoing clinical support. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h1)

question: When do patients most commonly move into a skilled nursing facility?

options.A: When they want to change their primary care physician
options.B: Immediately following a hospital stay for acute illness or surgery
options.C: Right after receiving a routine annual checkup from a family doctor
options.D: Before an elective outpatient procedure scheduled next month

explanation: Most patients step down from the hospital to an SNF when they still need professional nursing care before heading back home. Great clinical insight! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h1)

question: Which healthcare professional helps residents recover their ability to do everyday tasks like dressing and bathing?
explanation: Occupational therapy helps patients regain everyday self-care skills so they can live as independently as possible. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h2)

question: A resident needs daily sterile dressing changes for a deep surgical wound. Which facility type is best suited for this care?
explanation: Complex sterile wound care requires the expert clinical hands and continuous monitoring found in a skilled nursing facility. Spot on! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h2)

question: What is typically required by health insurance or Medicare to cover a stay in a skilled nursing facility?

options.A: A mandatory surgical procedure of any kind
options.B: Proof of full private health insurance coverage
options.C: A written referral from a public health minister
options.D: A qualifying hospital stay of at least three days

explanation: Insurance rules usually require at least three consecutive inpatient hospital days before they will help cover skilled nursing care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h3)

question: A patient wants to enter an SNF simply because they feel lonely at home and need help cooking meals. Why might this admission be delayed or denied coverage?

options.A: Social workers are not allowed to review home situations
options.B: The patient lacks a need for daily skilled nursing or therapy services
options.C: Medicare covers custodial care for anyone requesting it
options.D: The facility only accepts patients with infectious diseases

explanation: SNF coverage is meant for active medical or therapy needs, rather than basic social support or housekeeping help. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h3)

question: Who is usually the first member of the nursing team to notice small, daily changes in a resident's condition?
explanation: Certified nursing assistants (CNAs) spend the most time with residents, making them amazing at spotting early signs of a change in health! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h4)

question: Why is regular communication between nursing assistants and registered nurses so important in an SNF?

options.A: Registered nurses need assistants to write formal medical diagnoses
options.B: Registered nurses only work during night shifts
options.C: Nursing assistants report early warning signs like skin breakdown to the RN
options.D: Nursing assistants are legally required to manage all IV therapy

explanation: Teamwork is key! When assistants share what they see, the RN can step in early before a small issue becomes a big problem. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h4)

question: Which team member takes the lead in evaluating a resident's nutrition and managing special diets?
explanation: Registered dietitians assess nutrition needs, track weight changes, and design healthy meal plans tailored to each resident. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of regular team meetings among different healthcare professionals in an SNF?

options.A: To coordinate diverse professional insights and prevent conflicting care plans
options.B: To reduce the number of visitors allowed in the facility
options.C: To allow administrators to review employee attendance records
options.D: To replace the need for daily nursing assessments and vital sign checks

explanation: When nursing, therapy, and kitchen staff meet together, everyone works toward the exact same patient goals. Teamwork makes the dream work! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of the Minimum Data Set (MDS) assessment tool in a skilled nursing facility?

options.A: To calculate monthly billing statements for the facility kitchen
options.B: To schedule daily transportation for outpatient doctor visits
options.C: To replace physician progress notes in the main chart
options.D: To serve as a standardized assessment tool driving the care plan

explanation: The MDS is a comprehensive evaluation tool that helps nurses track a resident's health and guide their personalized care plan. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h6)

question: A nurse notices a resident's memory and thinking have suddenly gotten worse over two days. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the next scheduled quarterly MDS review to mention the change
options.B: Perform a focused assessment and document the changes clearly in the clinical record
options.C: Remove the resident from the care plan entirely
options.D: Update the facility menu without notifying the medical provider

explanation: Sudden health changes always require quick evaluation and clear, accurate charting so doctors can step in right away. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the main goal of restorative nursing care in an SNF?

options.A: To reinforce therapy goals during everyday routine activities
options.B: To administer complex intravenous medications overnight
options.C: To replace formal physical therapy sessions entirely
options.D: To manage facility financial records and insurance claims

explanation: Restorative nursing helps residents practice their therapy skills during daily routines so they can hold onto their independence. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why are gentle range-of-motion exercises and turning schedules crucial for residents who cannot move much on their own?

options.A: To speed up the metabolic rate and cure underlying chronic infections
options.B: To prevent secondary complications like contractures and pressure injuries
options.C: To eliminate the need for any nutritional support or dietary supplements
options.D: To guarantee that the resident will never need assistance walking again

explanation: Moving and turning patients keeps their joints flexible and protects their skin from painful pressure sores. Excellent nursing practice! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h7)

question: Which agency sets and enforces the main federal regulations for skilled nursing facilities?
explanation: CMS oversees the federal rules and quality standards that certified skilled nursing facilities must follow. You're building a strong regulatory foundation! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a focus area during a health inspection survey in an SNF?

options.A: Infection control practices and hand hygiene compliance
options.C: Stock market investments of the facility parent corporation
options.D: Resident rights and protection from abuse or neglect

explanation: Health inspectors look at patient safety, care quality, and resident rights—not corporate financial portfolios! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h8)

question: When should discharge planning ideally begin for a resident admitted to an SNF?
explanation: Starting discharge planning right away ensures home support and equipment are ready well before the patient leaves. Smart nursing starts early! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h9)

question: What is the biggest risk of a poorly planned transition when a resident leaves the SNF to go back home?

options.A: An avoidable hospital readmission due to lack of preparation
options.B: Immediate disciplinary action against the resident by Medicare
options.C: A mandatory extension of the SNF stay for two full years
options.D: The automatic cancellation of all future doctor appointments

explanation: Without clear medication guides and home help, discharged patients often suffer setbacks that send them right back to the hospital. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h9)
